belief: I'll pass this on and ruin my children's lives.
origins: Parents with inherited conditions often carry deep guilt about the possibility of passing them on. Some avoid having children, and some blame themselves for a child’s struggles.
teaches: “Children are indeed a heritage from the LORD, and the fruit of the womb is His reward.” “From everlasting to everlasting the loving devotion of the LORD extends to those who fear Him, and His righteousness to their children’s children.” A child’s life is in God’s hands, not only in genetics. Many children of parents with conditions are loved, helped, and flourish, and you can model faith and resilience. Guilt is not required of you. Love, honesty, and good care are.
self_statements: It is my fault if they struggle.
I should not have had children.
They will suffer because of me.
errors: Believing I am either a perfect parent or a harmful one.
Predicting that my children will suffer.
Feeling guilty and concluding that I harmed them.
questions: What exactly do I fear for my children?
What strengths and love am I also passing on?
What help and treatment would my children have available?
Have I shared honestly with them at the right level?
What does Scripture say about children and God’s care?
Whom can I talk to about my guilt?
truth: My children are God’s heritage and in His care. I pass on love, faith, and resilience as well as genes. I can seek good care for them and release guilt that is not mine to carry.
hw_truths: Children are a heritage from the LORD.
God’s love reaches their children’s children.
I pass on love and faith too.
Guilt is not mine to carry.
log: Each week, note one way you showed love or faith to your child.
actions: Write the strengths you pass on.
Talk with your children in age-appropriate ways.
prayer: Father, I fear for my children. Forgive my guilt, hold them in Your care, and help me pass on love and faith. Amen.
